newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Coca-Cola optimistic on EU probe of venture.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola optimistic on EU probe of venture.

text.p: U.S. soft drinks giant Coca-Cola said on Monday it was optimistic that the European Commission would approve in September its Nordic bottling and distribution venture with Danish brewer Carlsberg.
The European Union executive, which launched an in-depth review of the deal in May, is due to decide by mid-September whether to allow it to go ahead.
"We are cooperating with the Commission... and we're optimistic that it will be an approval in September," Shelagh Kerr, director of communication for Coca-Cola in Europe, told Reuters.

Last Tuesday, a senior executive of Swedish brewer Spendrups said that the European Commission should not sanction the planned alliance between Carlsberg and Coca-Cola because it would harm competition on the market.
Deputy Managing Director Ulf Spendrup told Reuters that Spendrups, the Swedish local partner of Pepsi Cola, had expressed its opposition to the deal in talks with the Commission.

In opening its detailed inquiry in early May, the Commission said it wanted to address concerns that the venture, Coca Cola Nordic Beverages A/S, could harm competition on the Danish and Swedish soft drink markets.
The venture would integrate the soft drink activities of Coca Cola and Carlsberg, first in Denmark and Sweden and eventually in the whole of the Nordic and Baltic regions.
It also involves licence agreements and a distribution joint venture with the Swedish brewer Falcon, which is jointly owned by Carlsberg and the Finnish brewing company Sinebrychoff.
